taylorConeEquilibrium.parameters: epsilon_0 = 8.854e-12 F/m (permittivity of vacuum), E = V_applied / d_gap (electric field strength kV/m), gamma_surface = surface tension (N/m)
taylorConeEquilibrium.explanation: Defines the mechanical balance between electrostatic Maxwell normal stress pulling the droplet into a conical geometry and capillary Laplace surface tension resisting deformation at the critical Taylor half-angle theta = 49.3 degrees.

scco2ViscosityReduction.formula: eta_scco2(P, T) = eta_0 * exp(-alpha * x_CO2(P, T))
scco2ViscosityReduction.parameters: eta_0 = neat biopolymer solution viscosity, alpha = plasticization coupling coefficient (~0.12–0.18), x_CO2 = dissolved CO2 mass fraction (typically 6% to 18% at 90–140 bar)
scco2ViscosityReduction.explanation: Supercritical carbon dioxide dissolves molecularly between biopolymer chains, acting as a molecular spacer and lubricator that lowers the glass transition temperature Tg and reduces zero-shear viscosity by 65% to 85% without adding toxic solvents.

nanofiberDiameterScaling.parameters: Q_flow = volumetric flow rate per nozzle (m^3/s), gamma_surface = surface tension, rho_fluid = density (kg/m^3), kappa_cond = electrical conductivity (S/m), I_jet = total transmitted jet electric current (A)
nanofiberDiameterScaling.explanation: Calculates the final dried sub-micron nanofiber diameter resulting from continuous electrostatic whipping, radial elongation, and dense-phase CO2 micro-expansion.

probioticSurvivalKinetics.formula: S_probiotic = N_viable / N_initial = exp( - (k_thermal * t_dwell + k_osmotic * Delta_Pi + k_shear * gamma_dot) )
probioticSurvivalKinetics.parameters: At 32–35°C (scCO2 operating range), k_thermal is essentially zero, while dense CO2 exposure time is kept below critical cell wall rupture thresholds (< 120 s), preserving >98% viability.
probioticSurvivalKinetics.explanation: Models the survival kinetics of probiotic cells during electrospinning, demonstrating that mild supercritical CO2 operating temperatures prevent heat-shock denaturation seen in spray-drying.

specificEnergyConsumption.typicalRange: 0.42 to 0.78 kWh / kg for scCO2-ESN vs 3.50 to 5.20 kWh / kg for thermal spray drying
specificEnergyConsumption.explanation: Calculates the total electrical operating power required per kilogram of dry nanofiber encapsulation web, demonstrating an 82% to 88% energy savings relative to thermal evaporation.
